method: nm -DC / readelf -sW --dyn-syms for the dynamic symbol table (address+size); llvm-objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn over the whole .text section (one pass, 649345 instruction lines) sliced per-symbol by [address,address+size); a small Python ARM64 pattern-scanner walks each method's instruction slice tracking 'adrp xN,#page' then the next 'add xN,xN,#imm' or 'ldr/ldrb xM,[xN,#imm]' touching the same register, computing resolved = page+imm; resolved addresses falling inside the .rodata VMA range [0xffd30,0x18c11c) are read as C-strings from a local copy of the section bytes (readelf/dd equivalent, section VMA==file offset for both .text and .rodata in this binary, verified via readelf -S). Strings matching /^AT[+-&A-Z0-9]/ are counted as AT command templates; strings matching /^\+[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,15}(:|=|$)/ are counted as URC/response-prefix candidates. This mechanical pass was run uniformly across all 39 handler classes (1026 exported FUNC methods); Tier-A classes got this automated per-method treatment across every method (this IS the full adrp/add cross-reference described in the task, applied programmatically rather than by hand, and its output was spot-checked by fully re-reading the raw disassembly for ~10 methods spanning most Tier-A classes plus the boot-handshake functions -- all spot checks matched the automated result). Tier-B classes got the same automated pass for coverage/listing purposes but were NOT individually hand-verified except for the ~8 methods flagged manually_spot_verified=true.
binary: vendor/lib64/libmtk-ril.so, ELF64 aarch64, 4833016 bytes, dynamic symbols intact (readelf --dyn-syms: 10703 entries, 10163 defined), stripped of .symtab/.debug_info. .text=[0x1e6000,0x460204) size 0x27a204; .rodata=[0xffd30,0x18c11c) size 0x8c3ec, flags AMS (alloc+merge+strings) i.e. this section IS the string-literal pool. VMA==file offset for both .text and .rodata (delta 0), confirmed via readelf -SW.
handler_class_count_note: The task prompt says '37' handlers but lists 39 distinct class names (recounted); nm -DC confirms all 39 are present and exported with real methods, so all 39 were processed. 20 of them match the prompt's explicit Tier-A list; the remaining 19 were treated as Tier B.

AT+ESIMS.evidence: adrp x1,#0x11c000 @0x424fcc; add x1,x1,#0x48d @0x424fd0 -> .rodata 0x11c48d = "AT+ESIMS=1"; passed to RfxBaseHandler::atSendCommand(this,cmd,0) at 0x424fe0. Sent unconditionally right after the object's RfxMclStatusManager setValue() call, i.e. at RmcRadioRequestHandler construction time (radio-domain bring-up).
AT+ESIMS.note: A second, bare 'AT+ESIMS' (no '=1') string also exists in the same .rodata merge pool at a nearby offset and is referenced elsewhere in the same constructor's string list (see RmcRadioRequestHandler ctor entry in at-map for the full ~15-command boot sequence found in this one function: AT+EBOOT=1, AT+CMEE=1, AT+CMER=1,0,0,2,0, AT+ICCID=1, AT+ESIMS=1, AT+ECFGSET="disable_sms","0|1", AT+ESBP=5,"SBP_ETWS_FOR_AOSP_DESIGN",1, AT+ESBP=5,"SBP_TERMINAL_CAPABILITY_FLEX",1, AT+CSCS="UCS2", AT+EDSDA=1, AT+EPOC, AT+EFUN=0, AT+ESLOTSINFO=1, plus calls out to sendERAT()/sendEGRAT() which send AT+ERAT=%d / AT+EGRAT=%d).

AT+EIND.note: Literal token 'AT+EIND' does not occur anywhere in .rodata (574444 bytes scanned). No handler references it. This guessed name from the task prompt is not used by this binary.

AT+EMDSTATUS.note: Literal token 'AT+EMDSTATUS' does not occur anywhere in .rodata. Not used by this binary. (A related-looking real command that IS present is 'AT+EMDT' -- modem power/task control, sent by RmcModemRequestHandler::requestModemPowerOff -- and 'AT+EMDVER' -- modem version -- but neither matches the guessed name.)

AT+ECSRA.evidence: adrp x1,#0x14b000 @0x335454 / adrp x2,#0x141000 @0x33545c; add x2,x2,#0x4f8 @0x335460 -> .rodata 0x1414f8 = "AT+ECSRA=1" (this second string is a log-format arg for the atSendCommand call at 0x335434, whose actual command-string operand is resolved via adrp x1,#0x149000/add x1,x1,#0x25 @0x335420/335424 -> 0x149025 = "AT+ECSRA=1\0%s,isEnableBearerNotification=%d\0ims\0[%d][%s] send %s"). Sent via RfxBaseHandler::atSendCommand(this,'AT+ECSRA=1',0) inside worldPhoneInitialize(), which is the RIL's multi-mode/world-phone bring-up routine.
AT+ECSRA.note: Also cross-referenced: RmcWpRequestHandler exports a static data object 'RmcWpRequestHandler::ecsraUrcParams' (20 bytes, .data, address 0x49c5f4) which looks like a parameter table tied to the ECSRA URC/response, consistent with ECSRA being part of the WP (world-phone) bring-up/URC-enable handshake.

AT+ESBP.attributed_to: RmcCapabilitySwitchRequestHandler::queryKeep3GMode()  [address 0x3055a8], and RmcRadioRequestHandler's constructor also sends two different AT+ESBP variants (see below)
AT+ESBP.evidence: adrp x1,#0x100000 @0x3055d4; add x1,x1,#0xc3d @0x3055d8 -> .rodata 0x100c3d = "AT+ESBP=7,\"SBP_GEMINI_LG_WG_MODE\"", sent via RfxBaseHandler::atSendCommandSingleline(this, cmd, '+ESBP:'-like response-prefix arg in x2, &respPtr) at 0x3055ec, response then parsed with atTokStart/atTokNextint.
AT+ESBP.note: RmcRadioRequestHandler's constructor (the boot-handshake function, see AT+ESIMS entry) additionally sends 'AT+ESBP=5,"SBP_ETWS_FOR_AOSP_DESIGN",1' and 'AT+ESBP=5,"SBP_TERMINAL_CAPABILITY_FLEX",1' at bring-up -- ESBP ('SIM Behavior Profile'?) is used both as a boot-time SET command (mode 5, various profile flags) and as an on-demand QUERY (mode 7) by the capability-switch handler.
